audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Drafted a source-grounded, English restoration of 2 Chronicles 30 (KJV verse numbering). Divine name יהוה rendered as YHWH. Preserves second-month Passover, northern-invitation rhetoric, prayer effect, and ritual irregularities; flagged loci needing witness checks.

verses.restored: Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, bidding them come to the house of YHWH in Jerusalem to keep the Pesach to YHWH, the God of Israel.

familiar.text: And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto the LORD God of Israel.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew text explicitly names Ephraim and Manasseh; 'house of YHWH' literal.

modern.text: Then Hezekiah sent word throughout all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh inviting them to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep the Passover of the LORD, the God of Israel.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וְגַֽם אִגְּרוֹת֙ כָּתַב֙ עַל אֶפְרַ֣יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לָב֥וֹא לְבֵית יְהוָ֖ה בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת פֶּ֔סַח לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: For the king, his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem resolved to keep the Passover in the second month.

familiar.text: For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, to keep the passover in the second month.

modern.text: For the king and his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month,

original.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֨ץ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֛יו וְכָל הַקָּהָ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַפֶּ֖סַח בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִֽי

verses.restored: They could not keep it at that season, for the priests had not consecrated themselves enough, and the people had not gathered to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, neither had the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew stresses lacking priestly sanctification and absence of the people.

modern.text: since they had been unable to observe it at the regular time, because not enough priests had consecrated themselves and the people had not been gathered in Jerusalem.

original.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֧א יָכְל֛וּ לַעֲשֹׂת֖וֹ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא כִּ֤י הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ לֹֽא הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמַ דַּ֔י וְהָעָ֖ם לֹא נֶאֶסְפ֥וּ לִֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: And the matter pleased the king and all the congregation.

familiar.text: And the thing pleased the king and all the congregation.

modern.text: This proposal pleased the king and the whole assembly.

original.text: וַיִּישַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָֽל

verses.restored: They issued a decree and proclaimed through all Israel, from Beersheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the Passover to YHWH, the God of Israel, at Jerusalem; for it had long not been done as written.

familiar.text: So they established a decree to make proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the passover unto the LORD God of Israel at Jerusalem: for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew emphasizes wide proclamation and that written prescription had been neglected.

modern.text: So they established a decree to circulate a proclamation throughout Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that the people should come to keep the Passover of the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem. For they had not observed it as a nation as prescribed.

original.text: וַיַּֽעֲמִ֣ידוּ דָבָ֗ר לְהַעֲבִ֨יר ק֤וֹל בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִבְּאֵֽר שֶׁ֣בַע וְעַד דָּ֔ן לָב֞וֹא לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת פֶּ֛סַח לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָרֹ֛ב עָשׂ֖וּ כַּכָּתֽוּב

verses.restored: So the couriers went with the king's letters through all Israel and Judah, according to the king's command, saying: 'Children of Israel, return to YHWH, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel; and he will return to the remnant of you that have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.'

familiar.text: So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Israel and Judah, and according to the commandment of the king, saying, Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.

modern.text: So the couriers went throughout Israel and Judah with letters from the king and his officials, which read: “Children of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, so that He may return to those of you who remain, who have escaped the grasp of the kings of Assyria.

original.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ הָרָצִ֨ים בָּֽאִגְּר֜וֹת מִיַּ֧ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֗יו בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּכְמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שׁ֚וּבוּ אֶל יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָם֙ יִצְחָ֣ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיָשֹׁב֙ אֶל הַפְּלֵיטָ֔ה הַנִּשְׁאֶ֣רֶת לָכֶ֔ם מִכַּ֖ף מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּֽׁוּר

verses.restored: And be not like your fathers and your brothers, who trespassed against YHWH, the God of their fathers, and he gave them up to utter desolation, as you see.

familiar.text: And be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the LORD God of their fathers, who therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see.

modern.text: Do not be like your fathers and brothers who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that He made them an object of horror, as you can see.

original.text: וְאַל תִּֽהְי֗וּ כַּאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ וְכַ֣אֲחֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָעֲל֔וּ בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם לְשַׁמָּ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתֶּ֥ם רֹאִֽים

verses.restored: Now be not stiff-necked as your fathers were; put out your hand to YHWH, and enter into his sanctuary which he hath sanctified forever; and serve YHWH your God, that the fierceness of his anger may turn from you.

familiar.text: Now be ye not stiffnecked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves unto the LORD, and enter into his sanctuary, which he hath sanctified for ever: and serve the LORD your God, that the fierceness of his wrath may turn away from you.

modern.text: Now do not stiffen your necks as your fathers did. Submit to the LORD and come to His sanctuary, which He has consecrated forever. Serve the LORD your God, so that His fierce anger will turn away from you.

original.text: עַתָּ֕ה אַל תַּקְשׁ֥וּ עָרְפְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם תְּנוּ יָ֣ד לַיהוָ֗ה וּבֹ֤אוּ לְמִקְדָּשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדִּ֣ישׁ לְעוֹלָ֔ם וְעִבְדוּ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְיָשֹׁ֥ב מִכֶּ֖ם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ

verses.restored: For if you turn again to YHWH, your brothers and your children will find mercy before those who carry them away, and will return to this land; for YHWH your God is gracious and merciful, and will not utterly turn away his face from you if you return to him.

familiar.text: For if ye turn again unto the LORD, your brethren and your children shall find compassion before them that lead them captive, so that they shall come again into this land: for the LORD your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew balances communal return with divine graciousness; implies political restoration.

modern.text: For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and sons will receive mercy in the presence of their captors and will return to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and merciful; He will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him.”

original.text: כִּ֣י בְשׁוּבְכֶ֞ם עַל יְהוָ֗ה אֲחֵיכֶ֨ם וּבְנֵיכֶ֤ם לְרַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י שֽׁוֹבֵיהֶ֔ם וְלָשׁ֖וּב לָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את כִּֽי חַנּ֤וּן וְרַחוּם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹא יָסִ֤יר פָּנִים֙ מִכֶּ֔ם אִם תָּשׁ֖וּבוּ אֵלָֽיו

verses.restored: And the couriers passed from city to city in the land of Ephraim and Manasseh even to Zebulun; and they mocked and scoffed at them.

familiar.text: So the posts passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun: but they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them.

modern.text: And the couriers traveled from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Zebulun; but the people scorned and mocked them.

original.text: וַיִּֽהְי֨וּ הָרָצִ֜ים עֹבְרִ֨ים מֵעִ֧יר לָעִ֛יר בְּאֶֽרֶץ אֶפְרַ֥יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְעַד זְבֻל֑וּן וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ מַשְׂחִיקִ֣ים עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וּמַלְעִגִ֖ים בָּֽם

verses.restored: Yet some men of Asher, Manasseh, and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem.

modern.text: Nevertheless, some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

original.text: אַךְ אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מֵאָשֵׁ֥ר וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וּמִזְּבֻל֑וּן נִֽכְנְע֔וּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Also in Judah the hand of God was to give them one heart to do the commandment of the king and of the princes, by the word of YHWH.

familiar.text: Also in Judah the hand of God was to give them one heart to do the commandment of the king and of the princes, by the word of the LORD.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew explicitly attributes unified will to the 'hand of God'.

modern.text: Moreover, the power of God was on the people in Judah to give them one heart to obey the command of the king and his officials according to the word of the LORD. Hezekiah Celebrates the Passover

original.text: גַּ֣ם בִּיהוּדָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ יַ֣ד הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֑ד לַעֲשׂ֞וֹת מִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: And there assembled at Jerusalem a great congregation to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month; a very large company.

familiar.text: And there assembled at Jerusalem much people to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great congregation.

modern.text: In the second month, a very great assembly gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

original.text: וַיֵּֽאָסְפ֤וּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַם רָ֔ב לַעֲשׂ֛וֹת אֶת חַ֥ג הַמַּצּ֖וֹת בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י קָהָ֖ל לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: And they arose and took away the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all the incense-stand altars they removed and cast into the brook Kidron.

familiar.text: And they arose and took away the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all the altars for incense took they away, and cast them into the brook Kidron.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew lists altars and incense altars; disposal into Kidron is literal in source.

modern.text: They proceeded to remove the altars in Jerusalem and to take away the incense altars and throw them into the Kidron Valley.

original.text: וַיָּקֻ֕מוּ וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ֙ אֶת הַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֵ֤ת כָּל הַֽמְקַטְּרוֹת֙ הֵסִ֔ירוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֖יכוּ לְנַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: They slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month; and the priests and Levites were ashamed and sanctified themselves, and brought the burnt offerings into the house of YHWH.

familiar.text: Then they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the second month: and the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and sanctified themselves, and brought in the burnt offerings into the house of the LORD.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew date is explicit: 14th of the second month; priests' shame and sanctification are linked.

modern.text: And on the fourteenth day of the second month they slaughtered the Passover lamb. The priests and Levites were ashamed, and they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁחֲט֣וּ הַפֶּ֔סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֤ם נִכְלְמוּ֙ וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ עֹל֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: They stood in their places according to their ordinance, as Moses the man of God commanded; the priests sprinkled the blood received from the hand of the Levites.

familiar.text: And they stood in their place after their manner, according to the law of Moses the man of God: the priests sprinkled the blood, which they received of the hand of the Levites.

modern.text: They stood at their prescribed posts, according to the Law of Moses the man of God. The priests sprinkled the blood, which they received from the hand of the Levites.

original.text: וַיַּֽעַמְד֤וּ עַל עָמְדָם֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם כְּתוֹרַ֖ת מֹשֶׁ֣ה אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ זֹרְקִ֣ים אֶת הַדָּ֔ם מִיַּ֖ד הַלְוִיִּֽם

verses.restored: For the multitude of the people had not sanctified themselves; therefore the Levites were over the slaughtering of the Passovers for all who were unclean, to sanctify them unto YHWH.

familiar.text: For there were many in the congregation that were not sanctified: therefore the Levites had the charge of the killing of the passovers for every one that was not clean, to sanctify them unto the LORD.

modern.text: Since there were many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves, the Levites were in charge of slaughtering the Passover lambs for every unclean person to consecrate the lambs to the LORD.

original.text: כִּי רַבַּ֥ת בַּקָּהָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם עַל שְׁחִיטַ֣ת הַפְּסָחִ֗ים לְכֹל֙ לֹ֣א טָה֔וֹר לְהַקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: For a great number of the people, many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not purified themselves; yet they ate the Passover contrary to the written rule. Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, 'May the good YHWH pardon everyone.'

familiar.text: For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good LORD pardon every one

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew states these tribes had not purified themselves yet were admitted; Hezekiah’s intercession follows.

modern.text: A large number of the people—many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun—had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover, contrary to what was written. But Hezekiah interceded for them, saying, “May the LORD, who is good, provide atonement for everyone

original.text: כִּ֣י מַרְבִּ֣ית הָעָ֡ם רַ֠בַּת מֵֽאֶפְרַ֨יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה יִשָּׂשכָ֤ר וּזְבֻלוּן֙ לֹ֣א הִטֶּהָ֔רוּ כִּֽי אָכְל֥וּ אֶת הַפֶּ֖סַח בְּלֹ֣א כַכָּת֑וּב כִּי֩ הִתְפַּלֵּ֨ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב יְכַפֵּ֥ר בְּעַֽד

verses.restored: And every one whose heart was prepared to seek God, YHWH, the God of his fathers, though he were not purified according to the purity of the sanctuary, was pardoned.

familiar.text: That prepareth his heart to seek God, the LORD God of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew emphasis on 'heart prepared' (lev) as basis for pardon despite ritual impurity.

modern.text: who sets his heart on seeking God—the LORD, the God of his fathers—even if he is not cleansed according to the purification rules of the sanctuary.”

original.text: כָּל לְבָב֣וֹ הֵכִ֔ין לִדְר֛וֹשׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֥ים יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֖א כְּטָהֳרַ֥ת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ

verses.restored: And YHWH hearkened to Hezekiah and healed the people.

familiar.text: And the LORD hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.

modern.text: And the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּרְפָּ֖א אֶת הָעָֽם

verses.restored: And the children of Israel who were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great joy; and the Levites and priests praised YHWH day by day, singing with loud instruments to YHWH.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness: and the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day by day, singing with loud instruments unto the LORD.

modern.text: The Israelites who were present in Jerusalem celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, and the Levites and priests praised the LORD day after day, accompanied by loud instruments of praise to the LORD.

original.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל הַנִּמְצְאִ֨ים בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אֶת חַ֧ג הַמַּצּ֛וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וּֽמְהַלְלִ֣ים לַ֠יהוָה י֣וֹם בְּי֞וֹם הַלְוִיִּ֧ם וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים בִּכְלֵי עֹ֖ז לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Hezekiah spoke comfortably to all the Levites who had good understanding of YHWH; and they ate throughout the feast seven days, offering peace-offerings and making confession to YHWH, the God of their fathers.

familiar.text: And Hezekiah spake comfortably unto all the Levites that taught the good knowledge of the LORD: and they did eat throughout the feast seven days, offering peace offerings, and making confession to the LORD God of their fathers.

modern.text: And Hezekiah encouraged all the Levites who performed skillfully before the LORD. For seven days they ate their assigned portion, sacrificing fellowship offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עַל לֵב֙ כָּל הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הַמַּשְׂכִּילִ֥ים שֵֽׂכֶל ט֖וֹב לַיהוָ֑ה וַיֹּאכְל֤וּ אֶת הַמּוֹעֵד֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֔ים מְזַבְּחִים֙ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֔ים וּמִ֨תְוַדִּ֔ים לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: And the whole assembly counseled to keep seven more days; so they kept seven more days with gladness.

familiar.text: And the whole assembly took counsel to keep other seven days: and they kept other seven days with gladness.

modern.text: The whole assembly agreed to observe seven more days, so they observed seven days with joy.

original.text: וַיִּוָּֽעֲצוּ֙ כָּל הַקָּהָ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִ֖ים שִׂמְחָֽה

verses.restored: For Hezekiah king of Judah had provided for the congregation a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; and the princes provided for the congregation a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep; and a great number of priests were sanctified.

familiar.text: For Hezekiah king of Judah did give to the congregation a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; and the princes gave to the congregation a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep: and a great number of priests sanctified themselves.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Numbers in Hebrew are explicit; note the combined royal and princely gifts.

modern.text: For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for the assembly, and the officials contributed a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep for the assembly, and a great number of priests consecrated themselves.

original.text: כִּ֣י חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְ֠הוּדָה הֵרִ֨ים לַקָּהָ֜ל אֶ֣לֶף פָּרִים֮ וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֣ים צֹאן֒ וְהַשָּׂרִ֞ים הֵרִ֤ימוּ לַקָּהָל֙ פָּרִ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וְצֹ֖אן עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֥וּ כֹהֲנִ֖ים לָרֹֽב

verses.restored: And all the congregation of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and all the congregation who came out of Israel, the sojourners who came from the land of Israel, and those dwelling in Judah, rejoiced.

familiar.text: And all the congregation of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and all the congregation that came out of Israel, and the strangers that came out of the land of Israel, and that dwelt in Judah, rejoiced.

modern.text: Then the whole assembly of Judah rejoiced along with the priests and Levites and the whole assembly that had come from Israel, including the foreigners who had come from Israel and those who lived in Judah.

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׂמְח֣וּ כָּל קְהַ֣ל יְהוּדָ֗ה וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְכָל הַקָּהָ֖ל הַבָּאִ֣ים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהַגֵּרִ֗ים הַבָּאִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַיּוֹשְׁבִ֖ים בִּיהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: So there was great joy in Jerusalem; for since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel there had been nothing like this in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was not the like in Jerusalem.

modern.text: So there was great rejoicing in Jerusalem, for nothing like this had happened there since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel.

original.text: וַתְּהִ֥י שִׂמְחָֽה גְדוֹלָ֖ה בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֠י מִימֵ֞י שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בֶן דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א כָזֹ֖את בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Then the priests and Levites arose and blessed the people; and their voice was heard, and their prayer went up to YHWH's holy dwelling place, even to heaven.

familiar.text: Then the priests the Levites arose and blessed the people: and their voice was heard, and their prayer came up to his holy dwelling place, even unto heaven.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew frames the blessing as audible and the prayer as ascending to YHWH's holy place.

modern.text: Then the priests and the Levites stood to bless the people, and God heard their voice, and their prayer came into His holy dwelling place in heaven.

original.text: וַיָּקֻ֜מוּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַלְוִיִּם֙ וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ אֶת הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשָּׁמַ֖ע בְּקוֹלָ֑ם וַתָּב֧וֹא תְפִלָּתָ֛ם לִמְע֥וֹן קָדְשׁ֖וֹ לַשָּׁמָֽיִם

translation_notes: Divine name: יהוה rendered uniformly as YHWH. 'Passover' renders Hebrew פֶּסַח (Pesach) as the ritual named in source.
Hebrew places and tribal names preserved (Beersheba, Dan, Kidron, Ephraim, Manasseh, Zebulun, Asher, Issachar).
Chapter reflects a delayed Passover (second month) and communal irregularities; prayer and royal initiative are shown as primary corrective acts.
safety_note: Contains religious coercion and ritual failure themes; no sanitization of morally difficult material.
